title: Feed a pencil into a moving sharpener while turning its crank
instruction: Sharpen the yellow pencil in the moving crank sharpener. Feed the pencil into the front opening while turning the rear crank clockwise, then withdraw the pencil and return it to its two rests. Let go and move both hands clear.
context: Manual pencil sharpening is recognizable household and classroom tool use. The physical coordination is simultaneous axial feeding of a loose workpiece and continuous rotation of a free-spinning crank knob by the other hand. A guided moving fixture provides a repeatable disturbance. Empty crank rotation earns no credit.
setup: Use the calibrated bimanual YAM station, with world X forward, Y left, Z up in metres; tabletop Z=0.7475 and arm bases at (0,+/-0.305,0.750). All initial body rotations are identity. Eight objects: (1) A 5.0 kg ballasted guided stage has body origin (0.245,-0.040,0.7625). Its base is 0.180 x 0.140 x 0.030 m; its support post is 0.025 x 0.050 x 0.055 m, offset (0,0,+0.0425) m. A world Y guide permits +/-0.020 m travel. The commanded Y is -0.040+0.005*sin(2*pi*t/8) m. (2) A 0.500 kg blue rigid sharpener housing, 0.060 x 0.070 x 0.070 m, is fixed to the stage at (0.245,-0.040,0.8675). Four rectangular bars form a genuine 0.009 x 0.009 m square through-aperture along X. The front face is X=0.215 m. (3) A 0.080 kg red crank carrier rotates freely about X at (0.285,-0.040,0.8675); it consists of an X-axis hub of radius 0.008 m and length 0.018 m, an 0.008 x 0.012 x 0.043 m arm offset Z=-0.0175 m, and an X-axis 0.003 m radius, 0.040 m long spindle offset (+0.020,0,-0.035) m. Passive angular damping is 0.020 N m s/rad, capped at 0.08 N m. (4) An 0.008 kg black free-spinning X-axis knob, radius 0.008 m and length 0.030 m, starts at (0.331,-0.040,0.8325), attached to the crank with a passive revolute joint; its damping is 0.0001 N m s/rad capped at 0.005 N m. Crank radius is 0.035 m. (5) The 0.005 kg grey cutter-face surrogate, 0.003 x 0.008 x 0.008 m, starts at (0.232,-0.040,0.8675). It is on a passive X slider relative to the housing, travel 0 to 0.006 m, spring 500 N/m, damping 3 N s/m, force cap 5 N, rest displacement zero. (6) A blunt yellow round wooden pencil, radius 0.0035 m, length 0.140 m and mass 0.006 kg, lies along X at (0.120,0.100,0.7810). (7-8) Two fixed grey 0.016 x 0.040 x 0.030 m rests are centred at (0.055,0.100,0.7625) and (0.160,0.100,0.7625). Generated geometry dimensions, joint anchors and fixture CAD are in assets/geometry.json and assets/fixture.scad. Start both grippers open in READY, seed 0, zero object jitter and motion phase zero.
scoring: End score is 0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 or 1.0. Loaded feeding requires whichever pencil end points toward the opening to lie in X=[0.229,0.242] m and within 0.0012 m of the actual cutter front face, transverse tip error below 0.0012 m, pencil-axis error below 5 degrees, and passive cutter displacement between 0.002 and 0.0065 m (nominal spring load at least 1 N). Track the two ends separately; partial cuts on opposite ends do not combine. Only actual crank revolutions during that condition count; counterclockwise motion subtracts from net progress down to zero. Award 0.25 once loaded feeding occurs, 0.5 after at least four net loaded clockwise turns, and 0.75 after eight. Eight loaded turns trigger the declared cutting-response approximation, showing a 0.020 m wooden cone and 0.003 m graphite point. Full score additionally requires the pencil centre within 0.015 m of X=0.120 and 0.012 m of Y=0.100, its lowest point Z in [0.7765,0.7815] m, axis within 10 degrees of either X direction, speed below 0.010 m/s, angular speed below 0.5 rad/s, and both TCPs more than 0.100 m away, continuously for one second. A pencil whose lowest point drops below Z=0.7175 m scores 0.0. Other outcomes receive their achieved material/feed tier or 0.0. Real-trial outcome checks use the visible intact point and pencil resting on both supports; marked feed depth and crank rotations can be checked from video. See assets/PROTOCOL.md for the surrogate-load interpretation and the difference between the simulation turn rule and real cutting quality.
run_limit: 1,600 control steps (80 simulated seconds at 20 Hz)
reset_notes: Return the carriage to its centre, reset the crank with the knob below the axle, unload the cutter spring and place a fresh blunt 140 mm pencil on the two rests. Restart the motion clock at phase zero and both arms in READY. Real trials consume one pencil and require removal of shavings; use an ordinary enclosed manual-feed sharpener on the moving plate. The supplied CAD describes the fixture and simulated geometry, not a functional printed cutter. A commercial tool source and the limits of product matching are documented in assets/PROTOCOL.md.
fidelity: Native contacts govern grasping, feeding and crank motion; only the stage is driven. A spring and passive damping represent nominal, unmeasured cutting loads. Eight loaded turns change the visible tip; the full pencil collider and mass remain. Teeth, shavings and fracture are omitted. Demo uses state feedback; Dream-1 uses standard cameras/joints. Inference pauses simulation. Detailed loads, approximations and real-tool limits: assets/PROTOCOL.md.
scores: Dream-1 beta run: 0.00; scripted native-contact demo: 1.00
